newsitem.title: USA: Houston Industries weighs FERC response.
newsitem.headline: Houston Industries weighs FERC response.

text.p: Houston Industries is still weighing a response to a federal inquiry into its merger with NorAm Energy Corp, chairman Don Jordan said on Monday.
The Houston-based utility holding company faces a Thursday deadline for responding to the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's assertion that it has jurisdiction over the merger, he said.
The two companies have said FERC has no regulatory role in the merger of the two Texas-based companies, but Jordan said disputing the federal agency's jurisdiction could delay the deal further.
"We really need to get this merger completed within a fairly short period of time," he told reporters after a speech to a Houston business group.
Houston Industries and NorAm are merging in a $3.8 billion deal that would form the nation's third largest combined electric-gas utility with 3.6 million customers in six states.
Jordan suggested the company is eyeing other deals as it prepares to compete in a deregulated electric industry, but he declined to discuss possible deals.
"We're going to be doing another deal here one of these days," he said.
